correctness.rationale: Straub–Moll–Amdeberhan equation (2.9) is an exact valuation identity. The 2-adic inverse of 3 minus 1 has digits 0,1,0,1,...; each floor difference is one outgoing carry, including the boundary after the last input digit. Enumerating both input digits gives E=[[2,0],[1,u]], O=[[1,u],[0,2u]], so T=EO=[[2,2u],[1,u+2u²]]. The odd-length tail weight [1,u] was separately derived. Resolvent inversion gives the two displayed rational generating functions. Differentiation gives exact means; the eigenvalues at u=1 are 4 and 1 and the dominant eigenvalue derivatives 4,4,16/3 give Gaussian centering and variance 2L/3+O(1). Exact recurrence arithmetic independently checks 4096 terms and all 13 block histograms; the universal proof does not extrapolate these.

originality.rationale: The 2008 primary paper proves the coefficient integrality, binary oddness condition, and individual valuation via carries, but its full accessible text does not give the complete dyadic valuation enumerators, explicit means, endpoint multiplicities, or Gaussian limit/variance. OEIS A004987 records the coefficient sequence and identities, not these distributional results. A generic digit-statistic central limit principle could cover the Gaussian part, and unlocated exact transfer-operator calculations remain a residual risk. The candidate is the nontrivial complete distribution, not a renamed pointwise valuation theorem.
residual_risks: The 2008 paper contains a general individual-valuation carry theorem; a full block-enumeration specialization may be considered routine by a later expert despite the new exact formulas.
A general automatic-sequence/additive-transducer theorem might imply normality with little further work; the exact rational enumerators and endpoint counts were not found in the inspected results.
Exact equivalent treatment in unlocated literature or sequence tables cannot be excluded by a finite search.

value.rationale: Montgomery–Shapiro and the follow-up 2008 study motivate understanding divisibility of the named three-central coefficients; the old result detects only valuation zero or each individual carry count. A two-parity rational spectrum gives exact frequencies at every valuation in every dyadic block, nontrivial boundary-tail asymmetry, exact means, sharp maximum multiplicities, and a normalized Gaussian law with explicit non-Bernoulli variance. This answers a natural distribution-level question rather than choosing arbitrary index slices or recomputing a known table.
